text.howto_turn: Use the matching next or previous sample at the rear blue control, with a free hand. Blue I identifies the same original driver, pin, rear arm and genuinely cutaway circular blocking member; orange O identifies the same original four-slot wheel. The original pin enters actual open radial notches, advances the wheel and leaves it dwelling while the input continues. Four concave recesses align with the cutaway blocking member during dwell; their positive clearance depicts indexed alignment, not physical restraint. The asymmetric pale output index stays attached to its original wheel and distinguishes all four stations. The red references and I/O labels stay fixed and mounted to the support frame. Sixteen configurations cover FOUR input turns and ONE opposite output turn. Within each driver turn the input samples are minus45,0,45,180 degrees: unequal45,45,135,135 degree increments, not uniform time or angle steps. Output advances minus45,minus45,0,0 degrees across these samples, showing entry, middle, exit and dwell. Both original assemblies remain rigid and connected; reversing follows the same coupled relation, and the full cycle restores all original geometry without resetting a quarter turn. Input and output shafts sit in genuinely hollow supported bearing sleeves. Natural depth and pin-head occlusion may hide joint faces; inspect the assembled mechanism from an oblique or side view. This is untimed indexed endpoint geometry only, with no continuous path/contact solver, force, friction, torque, power, physical security lock, output item, loose custody, autonomous timing or moving engine collision/support simulation.
